name: Passenger books a routed ride with profile contact
description: Verifies the main passenger booking flow uses the map, route search, profile phone contact, and direct browser routing.
steps: Sign in as a passenger
Open Request a ride and allow GPS or use the pickup field
Enter a destination and find the route
Verify the profile phone is shown as the ride contact without a Book for someone else control
Confirm and request the ride
Refresh the application
expected: The Mapbox map and route are visible, the profile phone is the default contact, the ride is created as Requested, and the app remains on a valid screen after refresh.

name: Passenger edits ride contact and cancels once
covers: cancelled ride removed from active trips
description: Verifies a passenger can edit the contact number for one ride and that cancellation removes the ride from active passenger views.
steps: Open the booking screen
Edit the ride contact number and save the edit
Request a ride
Open the active trip and cancel it
Return to the rider home or Trips screen
Attempt to find the cancelled ride among active trips
expected: The edited contact is used for the ride, cancellation succeeds once, the ride is no longer an active trip, and the cancelled ride cannot be cancelled again from the passenger active flow.

name: Passenger sees a proper not-found page
description: Verifies an invalid client route produces a dedicated not-found screen instead of silently opening the workspace home.
steps: Sign in as a passenger
Navigate directly to an unknown browser path, such as /this-route-does-not-exist
Observe the route result
Use the return action
expected: A dedicated 404 screen explains that the page was not found and provides a working return action.

name: Driver explicitly accepts or rejects a request
description: Verifies an authenticated verified driver can explicitly accept or reject a Requested ride without corrupting ride ownership.
steps: Sign in as a verified passenger and create a ride
Sign in as a verified online driver
Open Ride requests
Reject one request and confirm it disappears for that driver
Accept another Requested ride
expected: Rejecting records the driver rejection without cancelling the passenger ride, while accepting changes the selected ride to Accepted with the driver attached.

name: Passenger completes online Paystack payment and rates trip
description: Verifies a completed passenger ride can be paid online and rated once with durable state.
steps: Open a completed unpaid trip
Choose Pay online with Paystack
Complete the Paystack test checkout
Return to the Tridash trip route
Submit a 5-star rating with a short review
Attempt to submit another rating for the same ride
expected: Tridash verifies the exact fare and marks the payment Paid, the rating is saved once, the driver aggregate updates, and a duplicate rating is rejected.

name: Driver document verification requires checks before approval
description: Verifies driver onboarding stores documents privately, records automated checks when an authorised provider is configured, and does not treat uploads alone as proof of validity.
steps: Sign in with a driver account and open Driver verification
Enter first name, last name, optional other names, date of birth, phone, tricycle registration and operating state
Save the personal details
Accept the document-processing consent and upload a government ID, driving licence and vehicle registration
Confirm each upload appears with its current check status and no public storage URL
Sign in as an administrator and open Admin > Drivers
Open each document using the protected document route and record an official check result or a reason for rejection
Attempt to approve the driver before all required document checks are verified
Verify the backend rejects approval until all required documents are verified
Verify the driver cannot go online or accept rides before final approval
expected: Documents are stored outside public static assets, status and review audit fields are saved, missing or failed checks remain pending/rejected, and the backend blocks driver approval/online access until requirements pass.

name: Passenger cannot mutate protected ride fields
description: Verifies the generic ride update endpoint accepts only allowed status transitions and never trusts passenger-supplied ride fields.
steps: Create a Requested ride as a passenger and record its id
Send an authenticated PUT /api/rides/:id request as that passenger with status set to Completed
Repeat with driverId, amount, paymentStatus, paymentReference, and driverPhone fields
Fetch the ride again as the passenger or administrator
expected: Passenger update requests are rejected with 403; status, driver assignment, fare, payment status/reference, and contact records remain unchanged.

name: Public trip-share link returns only tracking-safe fields
description: Verifies an unauthenticated tracking link returns only the fields required by the shared-trip page.
steps: Create an active ride and generate a temporary trip-share link
Fetch its public shared-trip API endpoint without an authenticated session
Inspect every key in the returned ride and driver objects
Check for passenger phone numbers, driver phone numbers, home address, date of birth, payout/bank fields, and payment references
Try the link after expiry
expected: The response contains only route/status/fare/coordinates and minimal driver display/location fields. Private profile, contact, identity, payout, and payment data are absent; expired links return 404.

name: Two drivers cannot accept the same ride
description: Verifies the backend claims a ride atomically when two eligible online drivers attempt to accept it at nearly the same time.
steps: Create one Requested ride with no assigned driver
Sign in as two different verified online drivers with configured payout accounts
Submit both accept requests concurrently
Reload the ride from the API and inspect its assigned driver
Check that subscribers receive the successful assignment
expected: Exactly one request succeeds; the other receives 409. The ride has one assigned driver and cannot be reassigned by the losing request.

name: Keyboard and small-screen accessibility smoke test
description: Checks the core booking and confirmation experience without a mouse and at a narrow viewport.
steps: Set the viewport to 320px wide and check for horizontal page overflow
Navigate using only Tab and Shift+Tab and verify focus indicators remain visible
Use the skip link to reach main content
Open ride confirmation and verify focus moves into the dialog and remains inside it
Dismiss the dialog with Escape and confirm focus returns to the triggering control
Enable reduced motion and verify transitions/scroll effects are reduced
Inspect the map region and confirm it has an accessible name
expected: Core controls remain usable without horizontal page overflow, keyboard focus is visible and managed inside dialogs, the dialog can be dismissed with Escape, and the map has a meaningful accessible name.

name: Paystack settlement is reference-safe and idempotent
description: Verifies only the owning passenger can initialize or verify payment, and one confirmed Paystack transaction can settle a ride exactly once.
steps: Sign in as the passenger who owns a completed unpaid ride
Initialize a Paystack checkout and record its reference
Attempt verification from another passenger account and a driver account
Complete the test payment and return to the trip
Replay the same signed charge.success webhook
Attempt to settle the same ride using a different payment reference
expected: Only the owning passenger can verify the payment; the backend checks the exact reference, NGN currency, and expected amount; replayed events are idempotent; and a second reference cannot mark an already-paid ride as paid.

name: Passenger cancellation cannot overwrite a completed ride
description: Verifies cancellation is authorized for passenger accounts and uses a conditional status transition rather than overwriting a newer ride state.
steps: Sign in as the passenger who owns an active ride
Cancel the ride and confirm it is marked Cancelled
Try cancelling the same ride again
Repeat with a ride that has already reached Completed
expected: The first valid cancellation succeeds; duplicate or stale cancellation requests return a conflict; a completed ride remains Completed; and driver/admin accounts cannot use the passenger cancellation endpoint.

name: Driver and admin accounts cannot use passenger-only ride actions
description: Verifies sensitive passenger ride operations enforce the authenticated account role on the server, not just in the interface.
steps: Sign in as a driver and attempt to create a ride through the API
Attempt to cancel a passenger ride as a driver
Attempt to initialize or verify payment as a driver
Attempt to rate a completed ride as a driver
Repeat the restricted requests as an administrator
expected: The server returns 403 for passenger-only actions from driver and admin accounts, and no ride, payment, cancellation, or rating record is changed.

name: Repeated payment initialization resumes the same checkout
covers: checkout recovery after navigation or refresh
description: Verifies repeated initialize requests for one completed unpaid ride reuse the existing Paystack authorization URL and do not create another chargeable payment.
steps: Sign in as the passenger for a completed unpaid ride
Initialize payment and record the returned reference and authorization URL
Call initialize again before paying
Refresh the trip page and start payment again
Run two initialize requests concurrently for the same ride
Repeat with a legacy pending payment that has no stored authorization URL
expected: Normal retries return the same reference and authorization URL; concurrent requests are serialized; only one pending payment is created by this flow; a legacy pending payment is not silently replaced by a second reference.

name: Tridash refreshed palette and motion remain accessible
description: Checks the refreshed colour system and subtle transitions across the main passenger, driver and admin surfaces.
steps: Open passenger, driver and admin workspaces at 320px, 768px and desktop widths
Navigate all primary actions with the keyboard
Enable reduced-motion in the operating system and reload
Inspect the primary button, selected navigation, status labels and form fields
expected: The new charcoal/yellow/ivory/soft-green palette is consistent; key actions remain readable; keyboard focus is visible; layouts do not overflow horizontally; and animations are minimized for reduced-motion users.

name: Passenger dashboard layout and account activity
description: Verifies the approved passenger dashboard presents booking, active trip information, recent activity and account shortcuts without inventing trip records.
steps: Sign in as a passenger and open the home dashboard
Verify the welcome section and Book a ride action are visible
If an active ride exists, verify its current status and trip action are visible; otherwise verify the booking panel is shown
Verify recent trip rows match the passenger trip records, or that the no-history state is displayed
Open Trips, Safety and Profile using the dashboard shortcuts
Repeat at a 390px mobile viewport and a 320px narrow viewport
expected: The passenger dashboard remains consistent with the approved Tridash design, all shortcuts navigate to the correct screens, data reflects the authenticated passenger, and no horizontal overflow occurs on mobile.

name: Driver dashboard availability, performance and trip activity
description: Verifies the driver workspace presents operational status and metrics from the authenticated driver's own ride records.
steps: Sign in as a verified driver with a configured payout account and open /driver
Verify online/offline status and the availability action reflect the driver profile
Verify completed trip count, open request count, rating and completed fare value are derived from the driver's records
If the driver has an accepted or in-progress ride, verify the active trip panel is shown; otherwise verify the next-action state is shown
Open Ride requests and inspect the request queue
Open History and verify only the driver's assigned rides are listed
Repeat with a driver who is not verified or has no payout account and confirm the online action is disabled
Repeat at 390px and 320px mobile widths
expected: Driver data is scoped to the authenticated driver, availability is blocked until verification and payout prerequisites are satisfied, trip actions remain functional, navigation highlights the correct tab, and the layout remains usable on mobile.

name: Administrator operations dashboard and section navigation
description: Verifies the administrator console exposes all operations sections and that overview metrics reflect the records returned by the administrator APIs.
steps: Sign in with an administrator account and open /admin
Compare passenger, driver, active ride, pending verification, completed ride and open report metrics with the corresponding API records
Open Users and search for an account; verify role changes and suspend/reactivate controls remain available
Open Drivers and inspect verification applications and the registered driver directory
Open Rides and filter by Requested, Accepted, In Progress, Completed and Cancelled
Open Reports and verify incident records and the incident entry form
Open Payments and verify status and amounts match the payment API records
Open Settings and verify protected account-reset confirmation remains intact
Repeat navigation at a 390px mobile viewport
expected: All administrator sections load through their existing routes, metrics are calculated from returned records, search and ride filters work, protected actions retain confirmation, and mobile section navigation remains accessible.
